changed.from: For every fixed law in \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG},+}\), if \(t_n\downarrow0\), \(\sqrt n\,t_n\to\infty\), \(a_n\downarrow0\), and \(\sqrt n\,a_n\to\infty\), then \(\mathbb P(\widehat r_n=r)\to1\), \(\widehat\theta_n\to(\beta,A,\mu)\) in probability, and \(\mathbb P(\widehat G_n=G(A))\to1\). Fix \(p\), \(\Delta\), and \(\kappa\in(0,1/2)\). On \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)\), the geometric-mixing rate and eighth-bin-count envelope are conclusions of \(\text{lem:finite-depth-geometric-mixing}\) and \(\text{lem:uniform-bin-eighth-moment}\); assume only the remaining long-run-covariance nonsingularity and bandwidth conditions. Then \(\Phi_{\Delta,r(\theta)}\circ\mathcal C\) is basis-invariantly Fr\'{e}chet differentiable at \(\xi(\theta)\), with \(\mathcal J(\theta)=D(\Phi_{\Delta,r(\theta)}\circ\mathcal C)_{\xi(\theta)}\) and \(V(\theta)=\mathcal J(\theta)\Omega(\theta)\mathcal J(\theta)^{\mathsf T}\), and \[\sup_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}d_{\mathrm{BL}}\left(\mathcal L_{\theta}\{\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n-\theta)\},\mathcal N\{0,V(\theta)\}\right)\longrightarrow0.\] For every \(\varepsilon>0\), \[\sup_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}P_{\theta}\{\lVert\widehat\Omega_n-\Omega(\theta)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}>\varepsilon\}\longrightarrow0,\qquad \sup_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}P_{\theta}\{\lVert\widehat V_n-V(\theta)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}>\varepsilon\}\longrightarrow0.\]
changed.to: For every fixed law in \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{DAG},+}\), if \(t_n\downarrow0\), \(\sqrt n\,t_n\to\infty\), \(a_n\downarrow0\), and \(\sqrt n\,a_n\to\infty\), then \(\mathbb P(\widehat r_n=r)\to1\), \(\widehat\theta_n\to(\beta,A,\mu)\) in probability, and \(\mathbb P(\widehat G_n=G(A))\to1\). Fix \(p\), \(\Delta\), and \(\kappa\in(0,1/2)\). On \(\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)\), under the long-run-covariance nonsingularity and bandwidth conditions, rank selection is uniformly consistent and the structural estimator is uniformly root-\(n\) tight: \[\sup_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}P_{\theta}(\widehat r_n\neq r(\theta))\longrightarrow0,\] \[\lim_{M\to\infty}\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}P_{\theta}\!\left[\sqrt n\{ |\widehat\beta_n-\beta|+\lVert\widehat A_n-A\rVert_{\mathrm F}+\lVert\widehat\mu_n-\mu\rVert_2\}>M\right]=0.\] For every \(\varepsilon>0\), \[\sup_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}P_{\theta}\{\lVert\widehat\Omega_n-\Omega(\theta)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}>\varepsilon\}\longrightarrow0.\]
changed.reason: The current Gaussian claim is false at every absent unordered pair: the recovery formula contains \(z\mapsto\max\{z,0\}\), which is not Fr\'{e}chet differentiable at \(z=0\). The proposed claim retains rank adaptation, root-\(n\) estimation, HAC consistency, and support consistency, while moving normal inference to the algebraically smooth signed jump.

changed.from: For fixed \(p\), \(\Delta\), and \(\kappa\in(0,1/2)\), let \(W(\theta)=D\zeta_{\theta}V(\theta)D\zeta_{\theta}^{\mathsf T}=D\zeta_{\theta}\mathcal J(\theta)\Omega(\theta)\mathcal J(\theta)^{\mathsf T}D\zeta_{\theta}^{\mathsf T}\), where the same composite Jacobian is \(\mathcal J(\theta)=D(\Phi_{\Delta,r(\theta)}\circ\mathcal C)_{\xi(\theta)}\). Under the derived geometric-mixing and eighth-moment lemmas and the long-run-covariance nonsingularity and bandwidth conditions of \(\text{thm:rank-adaptive-estimation}\), \[\sup_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}d_{\mathrm{BL}}\left(\mathcal L_{\theta}\left[\sqrt n\left\{\zeta(\widehat\theta_n)-\zeta(\theta)\right\}\right],\mathcal N\{0,W(\theta)\}\right)\longrightarrow0,\] and \(\widehat W_n=D\zeta_{\widehat\theta_n}\widehat V_nD\zeta_{\widehat\theta_n}^{\mathsf T}\) is uniformly consistent for \(W(\theta)\). Gaussian-maximum calibration with \(\widehat W_n\) yields the simultaneous-coordinate guarantee \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}P_{\theta}\left\{\zeta_{ij}(\theta)\in I_{ij,n}\text{ for every }1\leq i<j\leq p\right\}\geq1-\alpha,\] and consequently \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}P_{\theta}\{G(A)\in\mathcal C_n(1-\alpha)\}\geq1-\alpha.\]
changed.to: For fixed \(p\), \(\Delta\), and \(\kappa\in(0,1/2)\), the composite \(\zeta\circ\Phi_{\Delta,r(\theta)}\circ\mathcal C\), evaluated through the signed jump before the positive-part edge map, is Fr\'{e}chet differentiable at \(\xi(\theta)\). Let \[W(\theta)=D(\zeta\circ\Phi_{\Delta,r(\theta)}\circ\mathcal C)_{\xi(\theta)}\,\Omega(\theta)\,D(\zeta\circ\Phi_{\Delta,r(\theta)}\circ\mathcal C)_{\xi(\theta)}^{\mathsf T}.\] Under the derived geometric-mixing and eighth-moment lemmas and the long-run-covariance nonsingularity and bandwidth conditions of \(\text{thm:rank-adaptive-estimation}\), \[\sup_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}d_{\mathrm{BL}}\left(\mathcal L_{\theta}\left[\sqrt n\left\{\zeta(\widehat\theta_n)-\zeta(\theta)\right\}\right],\mathcal N\{0,W(\theta)\}\right)\longrightarrow0,\] and the direct composite estimator \(\widehat W_n\) in the corrected \(\text{def:hac-estimator}\) is uniformly consistent for \(W(\theta)\). Gaussian-maximum calibration with \(\widehat W_n\) yields \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}P_{\theta}\left\{\zeta_{ij}(\theta)\in I_{ij,n}\text{ for every }1\leq i<j\leq p\right\}\geq1-\alpha,\] and consequently \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{\theta:P_{\theta}\in\mathcal M_{\Delta,p}(\kappa)}P_{\theta}\{G(A)\in\mathcal C_n(1-\alpha)\}\geq1-\alpha.\]
changed.reason: The chain-rule expression through \(D\Phi\) is undefined at absent edges, although the composite signed score is smooth because the two positive parts cancel exactly. The proposed statement drops the invalid factorization and retains the full signed-score Gaussian and graph-coverage conclusions.

changed.from: For an even Lipschitz kernel \(w\) supported on \([-1,1]\), set \(\overline Y_n=(n-2)^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{n-3}Y_k=\widehat\xi_n\) and \(\widehat\Omega_n=\widehat\Xi_0+\sum_{h=1}^{b_n}w(h/b_n)(\widehat\Xi_h+\widehat\Xi_h^{\mathsf T})\), where \(\widehat\Xi_h=(n-2)^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{n-h-3}(Y_k-\overline Y_n)(Y_{k+h}-\overline Y_n)^{\mathsf T}\). Set \(\widehat{\mathcal J}_n=D(\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}\circ\mathcal C)_{\widehat\xi_n}\), \(\widehat V_n=\widehat{\mathcal J}_n\widehat\Omega_n\widehat{\mathcal J}_n^{\mathsf T}\), and \(\widehat W_n=D\zeta_{\widehat\theta_n}\widehat V_nD\zeta_{\widehat\theta_n}^{\mathsf T}\).
changed.to: For an even Lipschitz kernel \(w\) supported on \([-1,1]\) and satisfying \(w(0)=1\), set \(\overline Y_n=(n-2)^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{n-3}Y_k=\widehat\xi_n\) and \(\widehat\Omega_n=\widehat\Xi_0+\sum_{h=1}^{b_n}w(h/b_n)(\widehat\Xi_h+\widehat\Xi_h^{\mathsf T})\), where \(\widehat\Xi_h=(n-2)^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{n-h-3}(Y_k-\overline Y_n)(Y_{k+h}-\overline Y_n)^{\mathsf T}\). Set \(\widehat{\mathcal J}_n=D(\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}\circ\mathcal C)_{\widehat\xi_n}\) wherever this derivative exists and \(\widehat V_n=\widehat{\mathcal J}_n\widehat\Omega_n\widehat{\mathcal J}_n^{\mathsf T}\). Define \(\widehat W_n=D(\zeta\circ\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}\circ\mathcal C)_{\widehat\xi_n}\widehat\Omega_nD(\zeta\circ\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}\circ\mathcal C)_{\widehat\xi_n}^{\mathsf T}\), evaluating the derivative through the smooth representative \(Z^*=K^*-(K^*)^{\mathsf T}\) before the positive-part edge formulas are applied.
changed.reason: Without \(w(0)=1\), even \(w\equiv0\) is allowed and the HAC estimator is inconsistent. The direct signed-score derivative is needed because the separate positive-part derivative of \(\Phi\) does not exist at absent edges.

changed.from: Let \(\zeta(\beta,A,\mu)=(\lambda_jA_{ij}-\lambda_iA_{ji})_{i<j}\), where \(\lambda=(I_p-A/\beta)^{-1}\mu\), so \(\widehat z=\zeta\{\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}(\mathcal C(\widehat\xi_n))\}\). Use the single composite Jacobian \(\widehat{\mathcal J}_n=D(\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}\circ\mathcal C)_{\widehat\xi_n}\), set \(\widehat V_n=\widehat{\mathcal J}_n\widehat\Omega_n\widehat{\mathcal J}_n^{\mathsf T}\), and estimate the covariance of \(\widehat z\) by \(\widehat W_n=D\zeta_{\widehat\theta_n}\widehat V_nD\zeta_{\widehat\theta_n}^{\mathsf T}=D(\zeta\circ\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}\circ\mathcal C)_{\widehat\xi_n}\widehat\Omega_nD(\zeta\circ\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}\circ\mathcal C)_{\widehat\xi_n}^{\mathsf T}\). Let \(I_{ij,n}\) be the resulting studentized intervals calibrated by the \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of the Gaussian maximum over \(i<j\). Then \(\mathcal C_n(1-\alpha)\) is the set of labeled acyclic graphs whose sign code \(j\to i\), \(i\to j\), or no edge is represented by a positive, negative, or zero value in every corresponding \(I_{ij,n}\). Define \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{fm}}(1-\alpha)\) as the simultaneous Wald ellipsoid centered at \(\widehat\theta_n\) with covariance \(\widehat V_n\).
changed.to: Let \(\zeta(\beta,A,\mu)=(\lambda_jA_{ij}-\lambda_iA_{ji})_{i<j}\), where \(\lambda=(I_p-A/\beta)^{-1}\mu\), and set \(\widehat z=\zeta\{\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}(\mathcal C(\widehat\xi_n))\}\). Estimate its covariance by the direct smooth-composite formula \(\widehat W_n=D(\zeta\circ\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}\circ\mathcal C)_{\widehat\xi_n}\widehat\Omega_nD(\zeta\circ\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}\circ\mathcal C)_{\widehat\xi_n}^{\mathsf T}\), with the derivative evaluated through \(Z^*=K^*-(K^*)^{\mathsf T}\) before positive parts. Conditional on \(\widehat W_n\), let \(c_{n,1-\alpha}\) be the \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of \(\max_{i<j}|\mathcal Z_{ij}|\) for \(\mathcal Z\sim\mathcal N(0,\widehat W_n)\), and set \(I_{ij,n}=[\widehat z_{ij}-c_{n,1-\alpha}/\sqrt n,\widehat z_{ij}+c_{n,1-\alpha}/\sqrt n]\). Then \(\mathcal C_n(1-\alpha)\) is the set of labeled acyclic graphs which, for every \(i<j\), use no edge only if \(0\in I_{ij,n}\), use \(j\to i\) only if \(I_{ij,n}\cap(0,\infty)\neq\varnothing\), and use \(i\to j\) only if \(I_{ij,n}\cap(-\infty,0)\neq\varnothing\). Define \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{fm}}(1-\alpha)\) as the simultaneous Wald ellipsoid centered at \(\widehat\theta_n\) with covariance \(\widehat V_n\) whenever that ellipsoid is well defined.
changed.reason: The former studentization is undefined for zero marginal signed-score variance and its factorization through \(D\Phi\) fails at absent edges. Unstudentized Gaussian-maximum calibration is defined for singular covariance matrices and uses the smooth signed jump directly.

changed.from: Set \(\widehat\xi_n=(n-2)^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{n-3}Y_k\), \(\widehat\eta_n=\mathcal C(\widehat\xi_n)=(\widehat m_n,\widehat\Gamma_{1,n},\widehat\Gamma_{2,n})\), \(\widehat r_n=\sum_{s=1}^p\mathbf1\{\sigma_s(\widehat\Gamma_{1,n})>t_n\}\), and \(\widehat\theta_n=\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}(\mathcal C(\widehat\xi_n))\) using any orthonormal basis of the truncated left singular subspace when \(\widehat r_n>0\); when \(\widehat r_n=0\), report the empty graph and leave \(\beta\) set-valued over \((0,\infty)\).
changed.to: Set \(\widehat\xi_n=(n-2)^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{n-3}Y_k\), \(\widehat\eta_n=\mathcal C(\widehat\xi_n)=(\widehat m_n,\widehat\Gamma_{1,n},\widehat\Gamma_{2,n})\), and \(\widehat r_n=\sum_{s=1}^p\mathbf1\{\sigma_s(\widehat\Gamma_{1,n})>t_n\}\). When \(\widehat r_n>0\), use any orthonormal basis of the truncated left singular subspace and set \(\widehat\theta_n=\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}(\mathcal C(\widehat\xi_n))\) if the resulting \(q\) lies in \((0,1)\), every inverse in \(\text{def:two-lag-inverse}\) exists, and every component of \(\widehat m_n/\Delta\) used as a divisor is positive. Otherwise report abstention and assign the fixed measurable sentinel \(\widehat\theta_n=(1,0,\mathbf1_p)\) solely to make the random tuple total. When \(\widehat r_n=0\), report the empty graph and leave \(\beta\) set-valued over \((0,\infty)\), again using the same sentinel for numerical asymptotic expressions.
changed.reason: The empirical moments need not lie in the population image: at finite \(n\), the estimated trace ratio can leave \((0,1)\), an inverse can fail, or an empirical mean divisor can vanish. A measurable fallback makes the estimator total without affecting any asymptotic result because the valid event has probability tending to one.

note: Accepted all 16 full-packet variants as one coherent faithful correction; both OEQs remain open. Follow-up totality, finite-sample PSD, optional full-map benchmark, and prose synchronization will be solver-authored through a scoped directive.

directive: Harden the accepted inference correction before D0 finality. Totalize the empirical signed jump z_hat, HAC covariance W_hat_n, Gaussian intervals, and graph-confidence set C_n on every abstention or invalid empirical-inverse event, explicitly inheriting the estimator sentinel/fallback. Ensure the finite-sample covariance passed to N(0,W_hat_n) is positive semidefinite by a declared PSD-preserving lag window, PSD-cone projection, or a conservative exceptional-event fallback, while preserving consistency. Remove, totalize, or explicitly restrict the optional V_hat_n/T_n^fm benchmark wherever the full positive-part derivative does not exist, especially in the boundary OEQ. Synchronize tldr, project_justification, related_work, definitions, and theorem prose so they distinguish the full-map root-n tightness from the signed-jump Gaussian/HAC route and do not claim a single full-parameter Jacobian. Reprove the affected nodes without altering the model class, identification kernel, or accepted lower-coverage/support-consistency statements.

changed.from: Set \(\widehat\xi_n=(n-2)^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{n-3}Y_k\), \(\widehat\eta_n=\mathcal C(\widehat\xi_n)=(\widehat m_n,\widehat\Gamma_{1,n},\widehat\Gamma_{2,n})\), and \(\widehat r_n=\sum_{s=1}^p\mathbf1\{\sigma_s(\widehat\Gamma_{1,n})>t_n\}\). When \(\widehat r_n>0\), use any orthonormal basis of the truncated left singular subspace and set \(\widehat\theta_n=\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}(\mathcal C(\widehat\xi_n))\) if the resulting \(q\) lies in \((0,1)\), every inverse in \(\text{def:two-lag-inverse}\) exists, and every component of \(\widehat m_n/\Delta\) used as a divisor is positive. Otherwise report abstention and assign the fixed measurable sentinel \(\widehat\theta_n=(1,0,\mathbf1_p)\) solely to make the random tuple total. When \(\widehat r_n=0\), report the empty graph and leave \(\beta\) set-valued over \((0,\infty)\), again using the same sentinel for numerical asymptotic expressions.
changed.to: Set \(\widehat\xi_n=(n-2)^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{n-3}Y_k\), \(\widehat\eta_n=\mathcal C(\widehat\xi_n)=(\widehat m_n,\widehat\Gamma_{1,n},\widehat\Gamma_{2,n})\), and \(\widehat r_n=\sum_{s=1}^p\mathbf1\{\sigma_s(\widehat\Gamma_{1,n})>t_n\}\). Use a fixed Borel-measurable singular-value-decomposition rule to choose the truncated left singular subspace and its orthonormal basis. For \(\widehat r_n>0\), compute every starred intermediate in \(\text{def:two-lag-inverse}\), and let \(\mathcal V_n\) be the event that \(\sigma_{\widehat r_n}(\widehat\Gamma_{1,n})>\sigma_{\widehat r_n+1}(\widehat\Gamma_{1,n})\), with \(\sigma_{p+1}=0\), the resulting \(q\) lies in \((0,1)\), every inverse in that definition exists, every component of \(\lambda^\star=\widehat m_n/\Delta\) used as a divisor is positive, and \(I_p-A^\star/\beta^\star\) is invertible; declare \(\mathcal V_n\) false when \(\widehat r_n=0\). Set \(\widehat\theta_n=\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}(\mathcal C(\widehat\xi_n))\) on \(\mathcal V_n\), and set the measurable sentinel \(\widehat\theta_n=(1,0,\mathbf1_p)\) on \(\mathcal V_n^c\). When \(\widehat r_n=0\), report the empty graph and leave \(\beta\) set-valued over \((0,\infty)\); when \(\widehat r_n>0\) but \(\mathcal V_n\) fails, report abstention. The sentinel is used only to make every numerical random object total.
changed.reason: The accepted fallback did not name one event inherited by downstream inference and did not ensure that the intensity appearing in the signed functional is defined. The corrected construction uses a measurable spectral rule, includes the rank-subspace gap and structural-intensity inverse among the validity checks, and assigns the sentinel on the entire complement.

changed.from: For an even Lipschitz kernel \(w\) supported on \([-1,1]\) and satisfying \(w(0)=1\), set \(\overline Y_n=(n-2)^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{n-3}Y_k=\widehat\xi_n\) and \(\widehat\Omega_n=\widehat\Xi_0+\sum_{h=1}^{b_n}w(h/b_n)(\widehat\Xi_h+\widehat\Xi_h^{\mathsf T})\), where \(\widehat\Xi_h=(n-2)^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{n-h-3}(Y_k-\overline Y_n)(Y_{k+h}-\overline Y_n)^{\mathsf T}\). Set \(\widehat{\mathcal J}_n=D(\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}\circ\mathcal C)_{\widehat\xi_n}\) wherever this derivative exists and \(\widehat V_n=\widehat{\mathcal J}_n\widehat\Omega_n\widehat{\mathcal J}_n^{\mathsf T}\). Define \(\widehat W_n=D(\zeta\circ\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}\circ\mathcal C)_{\widehat\xi_n}\widehat\Omega_nD(\zeta\circ\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}\circ\mathcal C)_{\widehat\xi_n}^{\mathsf T}\), evaluating the derivative through the smooth representative \(Z^*=K^*-(K^*)^{\mathsf T}\) before the positive-part edge formulas are applied.
changed.to: For the Bartlett kernel \(w(x)=(1-|x|)_+\), set \(\overline Y_n=(n-2)^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{n-3}Y_k=\widehat\xi_n\) and \(\widehat\Omega_n=\widehat\Xi_0+\sum_{h=1}^{b_n}w(h/b_n)(\widehat\Xi_h+\widehat\Xi_h^{\mathsf T})\), where \(\widehat\Xi_h=(n-2)^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{n-h-3}(Y_k-\overline Y_n)(Y_{k+h}-\overline Y_n)^{\mathsf T}\), with an empty inner sum interpreted as zero. This Bartlett matrix is positive semidefinite for every sample. On \(\mathcal V_n\), define \(\widehat W_n=D(\zeta\circ\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}\circ\mathcal C)_{\widehat\xi_n}\widehat\Omega_nD(\zeta\circ\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}\circ\mathcal C)_{\widehat\xi_n}^{\mathsf T}\), evaluating the derivative through the smooth representative \(Z^\star=K^\star-(K^\star)^{\mathsf T}\) before positive parts, and set \(\widehat W_n=0\) on \(\mathcal V_n^c\). On \(\mathcal V_n\) and only where the full derivative \(D(\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}\circ\mathcal C)_{\widehat\xi_n}\) exists, define \(\widehat V_n\) by its corresponding sandwich with \(\widehat\Omega_n\); otherwise set \(\widehat V_n=0\) as a numerical placeholder. The optional \(\widehat V_n\) is not used to define \(\widehat W_n\) or any graph interval.
changed.reason: A normalized lag window need not be positive semidefinite at finite sample size. Bartlett weights have an explicit Gram representation, while the piecewise definitions make both covariance objects total and keep the invalid full positive-part derivative out of signed-edge inference.

changed.from: Let \(\zeta(\beta,A,\mu)=(\lambda_jA_{ij}-\lambda_iA_{ji})_{i<j}\), where \(\lambda=(I_p-A/\beta)^{-1}\mu\), and set \(\widehat z=\zeta\{\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}(\mathcal C(\widehat\xi_n))\}\). Estimate its covariance by the direct smooth-composite formula \(\widehat W_n=D(\zeta\circ\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}\circ\mathcal C)_{\widehat\xi_n}\widehat\Omega_nD(\zeta\circ\Phi_{\Delta,\widehat r_n}\circ\mathcal C)_{\widehat\xi_n}^{\mathsf T}\), with the derivative evaluated through \(Z^*=K^*-(K^*)^{\mathsf T}\) before positive parts. Conditional on \(\widehat W_n\), let \(c_{n,1-\alpha}\) be the \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of \(\max_{i<j}|\mathcal Z_{ij}|\) for \(\mathcal Z\sim\mathcal N(0,\widehat W_n)\), and set \(I_{ij,n}=[\widehat z_{ij}-c_{n,1-\alpha}/\sqrt n,\widehat z_{ij}+c_{n,1-\alpha}/\sqrt n]\). Then \(\mathcal C_n(1-\alpha)\) is the set of labeled acyclic graphs which, for every \(i<j\), use no edge only if \(0\in I_{ij,n}\), use \(j\to i\) only if \(I_{ij,n}\cap(0,\infty)\neq\varnothing\), and use \(i\to j\) only if \(I_{ij,n}\cap(-\infty,0)\neq\varnothing\). Define \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{fm}}(1-\alpha)\) as the simultaneous Wald ellipsoid centered at \(\widehat\theta_n\) with covariance \(\widehat V_n\) whenever that ellipsoid is well defined.
changed.to: On \(\mathcal V_n\), let \(\widehat z\) be the vector of upper-triangular entries of the recovered signed jump \(Z^\star=K^\star-(K^\star)^{\mathsf T}\); on \(\mathcal V_n^c\), set \(\widehat z=0\). With the sentinel in \(\text{def:rank-adaptive-estimator}\), this gives the total identity \(\widehat z=\zeta(\widehat\theta_n)\). Let \(\widehat W_n\) be the total positive-semidefinite signed-score covariance in \(\text{def:hac-estimator}\). Conditional on \(\widehat W_n\), let \(c_{n,1-\alpha}\) be the \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of \(\max_{i<j}|\mathcal Z_{ij}|\) for \(\mathcal Z\sim\mathcal N(0,\widehat W_n)\). On \(\mathcal V_n\), set \(I_{ij,n}=[\widehat z_{ij}-c_{n,1-\alpha}/\sqrt n,\widehat z_{ij}+c_{n,1-\alpha}/\sqrt n]\), and let \(\mathcal C_n(1-\alpha)\) be the set of labeled acyclic graphs which, for every \(i<j\), use no edge only if \(0\in I_{ij,n}\), use \(j\to i\) only if \(I_{ij,n}\cap(0,\infty)\neq\varnothing\), and use \(i\to j\) only if \(I_{ij,n}\cap(-\infty,0)\neq\varnothing\). On \(\mathcal V_n^c\), set every \(I_{ij,n}=\mathbb R\) and let \(\mathcal C_n(1-\alpha)\) be the set of all labeled acyclic graphs. Define \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{fm}}(1-\alpha)\) as the full-parameter Wald ellipsoid only on \(\mathcal V_n\) when the full positive-part derivative exists and \(\widehat V_n\) makes that ellipsoid well defined; on every other sample set \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{fm}}(1-\alpha)=\overline\Theta_{\Delta,p}\). This optional parameter benchmark is not used in signed-edge or graph coverage.
changed.reason: The previous formulas were partial on the abstention event and the optional full-map ellipsoid remained undefined at absent edges. The correction gives the signed score, intervals, graph set, and benchmark explicit conservative fallbacks while retaining the accepted sign-inversion rule on valid samples.

State clearly that this covers cyclic, reciprocal, and self-exciting full-rank networks under no alias, while the existing DAG theorem covers singular rank and every Delta>0; do not substitute this narrower branch for the DAG kernel. directive: Extend covariance-only exact recovery from the DAG class to the entire current three-regime population union. Preserve the existing DAG covariance-only theorem and add image-defined covariance domains and maps for (i) the stable full-rank ambient principal-strip image and (ii) the nonempty stable zero-diagonal restricted-strip image, each defined as the population image under (Gamma0,Gamma1,Gamma2), never as arbitrary observable gates. Full-rank branch: from Gamma1,Gamma2 set T=Gamma2 Gamma1^{-1}, B=Delta^{-1}Log(T), J=B^{-1}(T-I), K=J^{-2}Gamma1, and Ctilde_+(t)=exp(Bt)K. Restricted branch: reuse O,R,F,L^sharp,H^sharp, which do not require m or D, and set Ctilde_+(t)=O exp(L^sharp t)(H^sharp)^2 R. Prove these equal C_+(t) on their domains. In both branches define D^0=Delta^{-1}[Gamma0-integral_0^Delta(Delta-t){Ctilde_+(t)+Ctilde_+(t)^T}dt] and m^0=Delta diag(D^0); use the general zero-lag covariance-measure identity to prove D^0=D=diag(lambda)>0 and m^0=m, then feed (m^0,Gamma1,Gamma2) into the already proved branch inverse. Prove every operation total, basis invariance for the restricted branch, representative independence, and strict non-DAG witnesses (cycle/reciprocal isolated examples plus a full-rank self-exciting example). Synchronize the covariance-only definitions/theorems, symbols, estimand overview, comparator covariance-only entry, tldr, project justification, related work, sampling/observation description, and honest scope so (Gamma0,Gamma1,Gamma2) is stated for all three recovery regimes. Do not extend sampling/inference beyond the acyclic fixed-margin class, do not treat this as one-lag recovery, and leave both sealed OEQs unresolved.

note: Accepted covariance-only recovery extension across all three population regimes after fresh gpt-5.6-sol/high adjudication; promote all four proofs.
Maximality round 4: proper active-block singular self-exciting regime, mean and covariance-only.
directive: Add a fourth population recovery regime for stable common-exponential Hawkes laws with a nonempty proper observed-label subset I, ordered coordinate selector E_I, and A=E_I A_I E_I^T where A_I>=0 is invertible, rho(A_I)<beta, mu>0, and spec(Delta(A_I-beta I_r)) lies in the principal strip. Labels outside I have no incoming or outgoing excitation but retain observed Poisson innovations. Define honest population-image domains for both (m,Gamma1,Gamma2) and (Gamma0,Gamma1,Gamma2), with exact recovery maps; do not claim observable membership beyond the image definitions. Prove S=im(Gamma1)=span{e_i:i in I} uniquely identifies I. Set E=E_I, F=E^T Gamma2 Gamma1^dagger E, L=Delta^{-1}Log(F), J_I=integral_0^Delta exp(Lu)du, K_I=J_I^{-1}(E^T Gamma1 E)J_I^{-T}. For the mean map use lambda=m/Delta, D_I=diag(lambda_I), solve LQ_I+Q_IL^T=-D_I, prove Q_I>0 and K_I=(beta^2 I_r-L^2)Q_I, recover beta=sqrt(r^{-1}tr(K_I Q_I^{-1}+L^2)), A=E(L+beta I_r)E^T, and mu=(I-A/beta)lambda. Prove totality, radicand positivity, canonical-coordinate/basis invariance, and representative independence. For covariance-only observation reconstruct C_+(t)=E exp(Lt)K_I E^T, recover full D and m from the proved zero-lag identity, then invoke the mean map. Include strict witnesses beta=1,A=diag(1/2,0),mu=1 and a 2x2 invertible reciprocal+self-loop active block embedded with an isolated label. Preserve all existing DAG, full-rank, zero-diagonal restricted-rank, and covariance-only theorems as complementary; update all population-regime/estimand/comparator/observation/project/related-work/honest-scope prose consistently. Keep sampling inference acyclic-only and both sealed OEQs open. Use beta=-tr(L)/r only for the zero-diagonal restricted branch; do not propagate any denominator typo from the audit summary.

note: Accepted proper active-block singular self-exciting recovery regime for both observation forms after fresh gpt-5.6-sol/high adjudication; promote all three proofs.
Maximality round 5: broad restricted-strip stable recovery via finite-bin covariance reconstruction plus Wiener-Hopf uniqueness.
directive: Add a broad exact-recovery regime covering every nonempty stable common-exponential Hawkes law with A!=0 and principal-log strip only on Delta(A-beta I) restricted to S=im(A), with no full-rank, zero-diagonal, coordinate-support, isolated-label, or invertible-active-block restriction. Define honest population images for both (m,Gamma1,Gamma2) and (Gamma0,Gamma1,Gamma2). For either image reconstruct r,S,O,R,F,L,H,K and the entire positive-lag covariance density C_+(t)=O exp(Lt)H^2R exactly from Gamma1,Gamma2, proving totality and basis invariance from the stable semigroup and restricted strip. Obtain D=diag(m/Delta) for the mean input, or recover D first from Gamma0 by the proved zero-lag identity for the covariance-only input. Define the complete conditional response with the exact orientation g(t)=C_+(t)D^{-1} for t>0 and g(t)=C_+(-t)^T D^{-1} for t<0. Add and citation-revalidate a precise BacryMuzy2016 Wiener-Hopf lemma using their Section II-B, Proposition 2 Eq.18 and Theorem 1 Eq.19: under the stable causal L1 Hawkes hypotheses, phi is the unique causal entrywise-L1 solution chi of g(t)=chi(t)+(chi*g)(t), t>0. Explicitly audit notation/orientation and do not claim the cited paper proves finite-bin reconstruction. Recover phi, then M0=int phi=A/beta, M1=int t phi=A/beta^2, u0=1^T M0 1>0, u1=1^T M1 1>0, beta=u0/u1, A=beta M0, lambda=diag(D), mu=(I-M0)lambda. Prove totality, exactness, representative independence, and covariance-only companion. Include strict witness beta=1, mu=1, A=(1/4)11^T, which is singular, self-exciting, reciprocal, non-coordinate-image, and restricted-strip admissible. Retain the existing four algebraic branches as explicit closed-form special cases and all sampling inference as acyclic-only. Update all population-regime/estimand/comparator/observation/project/related-work/honest-scope prose, stating Bacry-Muzy supplies only the full-response uniqueness step while this paper reconstructs that response from fixed finite summaries. Leave both sealed OEQs unchanged.

{"id":"def:wiener-hopf-two-lag-inverse","name":"Broad stable two-lag Wiener--Hopf inverse","construction":"For \(\eta=(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\in\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{WH}}\), set
\[
 r=\operatorname{rank}(\Gamma_1),\qquad S=\operatorname{im}(\Gamma_1),
\]
choose any \(O\in\mathbb R^{p\times r}\) with \(O^{\mathsf T}O=I_r\) and \(\operatorname{im}(O)=S\), and define
\[
 R=O^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_1,\quad
 F=O^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_2R^{\mathsf T}(RR^{\mathsf T})^{-1},
\]
\[
 L^{\mathrm{WH}}=\Delta^{-1}\operatorname{Log}(F),\quad
 H^{\mathrm{WH}}=L^{\mathrm{WH}}(F-I_r)^{-1},\quad
 K^{\mathrm{WH}}=O(H^{\mathrm{WH}})^2R,
\]
and, for \(t>0\),
\[
 C_{+}^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)=Oe^{L^{\mathrm{WH}}t}(H^{\mathrm{WH}})^2R.
\]
Set \(\lambda^{\mathrm{WH}}=m/\Delta\), \(D^{\mathrm{WH}}=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda^{\mathrm{WH}})\), and
\[
 g^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)=
 \begin{cases}
 C_{+}^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)(D^{\mathrm{WH}})^{-1},&t>0,\\
 C_{+}^{\mathrm{WH}}(-t)^{\mathsf T}(D^{\mathrm{WH}})^{-1},&t<0,\\
 0,&t=0.
 \end{cases}
\]
Let \(\chi^{\mathrm{WH}}\) be the unique matrix function whose entries are causal and in \(L^1(\mathbb R_+)\) and which satisfies
\[
 g^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)=\chi^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)
 +(\chi^{\mathrm{WH}}*g^{\mathrm{WH}})(t),\qquad t>0,
\]
where
\[
 (\chi^{\mathrm{WH}}*g^{\mathrm{WH}})(t)
 =\int_0^\infty\chi^{\mathrm{WH}}(s)g^{\mathrm{WH}}(t-s)\,ds
\]
uses ordinary matrix multiplication inside the integral.  Finally set
\[
 M_0^{\mathrm{WH}}=\int_0^\infty\chi^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)\,dt,\quad
 M_1^{\mathrm{WH}}=\int_0^\infty t\chi^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)\,dt,
\]
\[
 u_0^{\mathrm{WH}}=\mathbf 1_p^{\mathsf T}M_0^{\mathrm{WH}}\mathbf 1_p,\quad
 u_1^{\mathrm{WH}}=\mathbf 1_p^{\mathsf T}M_1^{\mathrm{WH}}\mathbf 1_p,
\]
\[
 \beta^{\mathrm{WH}}=u_0^{\mathrm{WH}}/u_1^{\mathrm{WH}},\qquad
 A^{\mathrm{WH}}=\beta^{\mathrm{WH}}M_0^{\mathrm{WH}},\qquad
 \mu^{\mathrm{WH}}=(I_p-M_0^{\mathrm{WH}})\lambda^{\mathrm{WH}}.
\]
Define
\[
 \Phi_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{WH}}(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)
 =(\beta^{\mathrm{WH}},A^{\mathrm{WH}},\mu^{\mathrm{WH}}).
\]","free_symbols":["PhiBroad","Ibroad","eta","m","Gamma","Delta","p","r","S","O","R","F","Lwh","Hwh","Kwh","Cwh","t","lambda","Dwh","gWh","chiWh","Mzero","Mone","uZero","uOne","beta","A","mu"],"inputs":["Ibroad","m","Gamma","Delta"]}

{"id":"prop:empty-graph-honest-diameter","kind":"proposition","statement":"Let \(\theta_a=(\beta_a,0,\mu_0)\), \(a\in\{0,1\}\), be two parameters in \(\overline{\mathcal M}_{\Delta,p}(\kappa_0)\) with a common strictly positive baseline and \(\beta_0\neq\beta_1\). \[
 P_0\!\left\{\operatorname{diam}_{\Theta}(\mathcal T_n)\geq1\wedge|\beta_0-\beta_1|\right\}\geq(1-2\alpha)_+.
\]
If \(|\beta_0-\beta_1|\geq1\), then the event in the display is \(\{\operatorname{diam}_{\Theta}(\mathcal T_n)=1\}\).","free_symbols":["theta","beta","A","mu","Ptheta","Mregular","Delta","p","kappa0","Un","HonestClass","alpha","G","diamTheta","rhoTheta","n"],"depends_on":["def:nuisance-regular-closure","def:parameter-law-topologies","def:boundary-risks","prop:empty-graph-equivalence"],"status":"proved","justification":"The proposition isolates the exact nonvanishing confidence-diameter obstruction caused by decay nonidentification at the empty graph.","gap":"The general Gleser--Hwang phenomenon does not itself give this bounded-metric two-decay witness for the Hawkes closure.","consumer":"It prevents an honest boundary procedure from reporting a spuriously narrow decay set at an empty network.","proof_tex":"By \(\text{prop:empty-graph-equivalence}\), the two empty-graph parameters induce the same law \(P_0\), because they have the same baseline \(\mu\) and their intensities contain no occurrence of the decay. \[
 P_0\{G(0)\in\mathcal G_n,\ \theta_a\in\mathcal T_n\}\geq1-\alpha.
\tag{1}
\]
Dropping the graph event in (1) gives \(P_0\{\theta_a\in\mathcal T_n\}\geq1-\alpha\).  The union bound therefore yields
\[
 P_0\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in\mathcal T_n\}\geq1-2\alpha.
\tag{2}
\]
On the event in (2), the definitions of \(\operatorname{diam}_\Theta\) and \(\rho_\Theta\) give
\[
 \operatorname{diam}_\Theta(\mathcal T_n)

For every such representative \((\beta,A,\mu)\),
\[
 r=\operatorname{rank}(A)\geq1,\quad S=\operatorname{im}(A),\quad
 F=[T|_S]_O,\quad L^{\mathrm{WH}}=[B|_S]_O,\quad
 H^{\mathrm{WH}}=[J|_S]_O^{-1},
\]
\[
 K^{\mathrm{WH}}=K,\quad C_{+}^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)=C_{+}(t)\quad(t>0),\quad
 D^{\mathrm{WH}}=D,\quad g^{\mathrm{WH}}=g,\quad
 \chi^{\mathrm{WH}}=\phi,
\]
\[
 M_0^{\mathrm{WH}}=A/\beta,\quad M_1^{\mathrm{WH}}=A/\beta^2,\quad
 u_0^{\mathrm{WH}}>0,\quad u_1^{\mathrm{WH}}>0,
\]
and
\[
 \Phi_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{WH}}(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)=(\beta,A,\mu).
\]
Thus the mean and two positive fixed-bin covariance lags identify the entire stable nonzero common-exponential Hawkes mechanism, and hence its labeled graph, whenever the principal-log strip holds only on \(S=\operatorname{im}(A)\); no full-rank, zero-diagonal, coordinate-support, isolated-label, acyclicity, or invertible-active-block condition is required.  The regime is strictly broader than each such algebraic special case: for \(p=2\), every \(\Delta>0\), \(\beta=1\), \(\mu=\mathbf 1_2\), and \(A=\tfrac14\mathbf 1_2\mathbf 1_2^{\mathsf T}\) define an admissible member whose \(A\) is singular, self-exciting, reciprocal, and has the non-coordinate image \(\operatorname{span}(\mathbf 1_2)\).

For every \(\eta=(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)\in\mathfrak I_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{WH}}\), every operation in \(\text{def:wiener-hopf-two-lag-inverse}\) is well defined, independent of the orthonormal basis \(O\), and independent of the admissible structural representative.  For every such representative \((\beta,A,\mu)\),
\[
 r=\operatorname{rank}(A)\geq1,\quad S=\operatorname{im}(A),\quad
 F=[T|_S]_O,\quad L^{\mathrm{WH}}=[B|_S]_O,\quad
 H^{\mathrm{WH}}=[J|_S]_O^{-1},
\]
\[
 K^{\mathrm{WH}}=K,\quad C_{+}^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)=C_{+}(t)\quad(t>0),\quad
 D^{\mathrm{WH}}=D,\quad g^{\mathrm{WH}}=g.
\]
Writing \(P^{\mathrm{WH}}=(H^{\mathrm{WH}})^2R\), the response transform is finite dimensional:
\[
 \mathcal R^{\mathrm{WH}}(x)
 =(P^{\mathrm{WH}})^{\mathsf T}(xI_r-(L^{\mathrm{WH}})^{\mathsf T})^{-1}O^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad x>0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \mathcal R^{\mathrm{WH}}(\beta)
 =K^{\mathsf T}(2\beta I_p-A^{\mathsf T})^{-1}=QA^{\mathsf T},
\]
\[
 D+\mathcal R^{\mathrm{WH}}(\beta)=(2\beta I_p-A)Q,
 \qquad A[D+\mathcal R^{\mathrm{WH}}(\beta)]=K,
 \qquad AO=O(L^{\mathrm{WH}}+\beta I_r).
\]
The pair \((\beta,A)\) is the unique \((x,M)\in(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R^{p\times p}\) satisfying
\[
 MO=O(L^{\mathrm{WH}}+xI_r),\qquad
 M[D+\mathcal R^{\mathrm{WH}}(x)]=K.
\]
Consequently \(\beta\in\Omega^{\mathrm{WH}}\), the scalar equation
\[
 \mathcal A^{\mathrm{WH}}(x)O=O(L^{\mathrm{WH}}+xI_r),\qquad x\in\Omega^{\mathrm{WH}},
\]
has the unique solution \(\beta^{\#}=\beta\), and \(A^{\#}=A\), \(\mu^{\#}=\mu\).  Hence
\[
 \Phi_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{WH}}(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)=(\beta,A,\mu).
\]
Thus the mean and two positive fixed-bin covariance lags identify the entire stable nonzero common-exponential Hawkes mechanism, and hence its labeled graph, whenever the principal-log strip holds only on \(S=\operatorname{im}(A)\); no full-rank, zero-diagonal, coordinate-support, isolated-label, acyclicity, or invertible-active-block condition is required. \[
 r=\operatorname{rank}(\Gamma_1),\qquad S=\operatorname{im}(\Gamma_1),
\]
choose any \(O\in\mathbb R^{p\times r}\) with \(O^{\mathsf T}O=I_r\) and \(\operatorname{im}(O)=S\), and define
\[
 R=O^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_1,\quad
 F=O^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_2R^{\mathsf T}(RR^{\mathsf T})^{-1},
\]
\[
 L^{\mathrm{WH}}=\Delta^{-1}\operatorname{Log}(F),\quad
 H^{\mathrm{WH}}=L^{\mathrm{WH}}(F-I_r)^{-1},\quad
 K^{\mathrm{WH}}=O(H^{\mathrm{WH}})^2R,
\]
and, for \(t>0\),
\[
 C_{+}^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)=Oe^{L^{\mathrm{WH}}t}(H^{\mathrm{WH}})^2R.
\]
Set \(\lambda^{\mathrm{WH}}=m/\Delta\), \(D^{\mathrm{WH}}=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda^{\mathrm{WH}})\), and
\[
 g^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)=
 \begin{cases}
 C_{+}^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)(D^{\mathrm{WH}})^{-1},&t>0,\\
 C_{+}^{\mathrm{WH}}(-t)^{\mathsf T}(D^{\mathrm{WH}})^{-1},&t<0,\\
 0,&t=0.
 \end{cases}
\]
Let \(\chi^{\mathrm{WH}}\) be the unique matrix function whose entries are causal and in \(L^1(\mathbb R_+)\) and which satisfies
\[
 g^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)=\chi^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)
 +(\chi^{\mathrm{WH}}*g^{\mathrm{WH}})(t),\qquad t>0,
\]
where
\[
 (\chi^{\mathrm{WH}}*g^{\mathrm{WH}})(t)
 =\int_0^\infty\chi^{\mathrm{WH}}(s)g^{\mathrm{WH}}(t-s)\,ds
\]
uses ordinary matrix multiplication inside the integral.  Finally set
\[
 M_0^{\mathrm{WH}}=\int_0^\infty\chi^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)\,dt,\quad
 M_1^{\mathrm{WH}}=\int_0^\infty t\chi^{\mathrm{WH}}(t)\,dt,
\]
\[
 u_0^{\mathrm{WH}}=\mathbf 1_p^{\mathsf T}M_0^{\mathrm{WH}}\mathbf 1_p,\quad
 u_1^{\mathrm{WH}}=\mathbf 1_p^{\mathsf T}M_1^{\mathrm{WH}}\mathbf 1_p,
\]
\[
 \beta^{\mathrm{WH}}=u_0^{\mathrm{WH}}/u_1^{\mathrm{WH}},\qquad
 A^{\mathrm{WH}}=\beta^{\mathrm{WH}}M_0^{\mathrm{WH}},\qquad
 \mu^{\mathrm{WH}}=(I_p-M_0^{\mathrm{WH}})\lambda^{\mathrm{WH}}.
\]
Define
\[
 \Phi_{\Delta,p}^{\mathrm{WH}}(m,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2)
 =(\beta^{\mathrm{WH}},A^{\mathrm{WH}},\mu^{\mathrm{WH}}).
\]

\[

\[
